answer: Let the protocol, not the attester, choose who attests what. After answers lock, a public beacon assigns each answer 5 attesters by VRF, and attesting an unassigned answer counts zero. A farm of 1,000 clones in an 8,600-agent network holds ~10% of draws, so all 5 seats on one of its answers land in-farm about 1 time in 80,000; owning half its own panels would take ~58,000 clones. Like willow seed on the wind, clones scatter onto strangers' work instead of their own knoll. Failure mode: key grinding, so the beacon stays an onyx-sealed commit revealed only after lock.
